references.title: Policy Logic Forge: compiling compliance policy text into typed, source-grounded executable decision logic
references.publication_or_version: Repository at commit c22dc450 (2026-09-11): ARCHITECTURE.md §§ 1.1, 2.1, 2.3, 2.4, 2.5, 5, 5.1, 6, 6.4; docs/ir-semantics-v1.md; docs/executable-models.md; docs/smt-query-protocol.md; technical-report/report.tex § Scope and limitations; and the modules and tests named in the supports text
references.supports: Book-authored implementation. Supports the existence in the repository at the pinned commit of the following architectural elements, each attributable only as what the named component does: a build-time, thirteen-stage, checkpointed extraction pipeline with no runtime consumer, whose exit-code contract distinguishes data-quality review from failure and in which a stage may never exit 0 for work it did not do (§§ 2.1, 2.4; cli/extract.py; tests/test_pipeline_end_to_end.py); per-chunk and per-corpus content digests and per-field source references with evidence spans whose offsets are excerpt-local (utils/kg_readiness.py; utils/rule_contract.py; docs/ir-semantics-v1.md); four deterministic readiness invariants gated on blocking defects alone, with evidence gaps held rather than failed (§ 2.3 agent_07; utils/kg_readiness.py); targeted remediation of only the failed fields (§ 2.3 agent_08); review routing in which only a positive contradiction or an explicit judgment finding enters the human queue, contract defects go to machine repair and evidence gaps to case management (utils/semantic_routing.py; docs/executable-models.md); independent claim-level grounding that rebuilds evidence from the corpus, admits a supported or contradicted verdict only when it names an evidence record resolved as literal corpus text, records the quote from that record, verifies derived values structurally, and treats verifier completeness as a fail-closed check distinct from verdict counts (§ 2.3 agent_09; agents/agent_09_grounding_verifier.py; utils/citations.py); a grounding certificate bound to the corpus and graph hashes, and intermediate results keyed by a content fingerprint and rejected when it changes (§ 2.5; agent_09 certification_issues); exact-duplicate merge with evidence union (§ 2.3 agent_06); typing from declared units and value sets with refinement reported separately from contradiction, model validation that reports and never repairs, and a fail-closed unresolved concept kind in an SBVR-aligned vocabulary profile that is explicitly not full interchange (§ 2.3 agent_12; § 6.4; utils/information_model.py); fail-closed lowering in which a rule is emitted completely or refused with a typed reason, Kleene three-valued evaluation in which a missing input is unknown and unknown at a table boundary means refuse, a conflict between rules refused rather than adjudicated, decision-table hit-policy obligations proved by bounded enumeration on finite domains with unknown and timeout never a pass, and refusal of any rule whose scope needs jurisdiction, party or date context the evaluator does not have (docs/ir-semantics-v1.md; docs/smt-query-protocol.md; utils/feel.py; tests/test_feel.py; tests/test_hit_policy_proofs.py); fail-closed DMN and BPMN projections in which BPMN is emitted only for source-explicit ordered process semantics (§ 6; utils/executable_models.py; utils/semantic_routing.py); version-to-version change detection that aligns rules by exact id then by unique source citation, classifies change ignoring provenance, propagates impact over the dependency graph, resolves every rule to exactly one of changed, unchanged, unresolved-review or refused with held rules never auto-resolved and kept in every denominator, and states full replay as the oracle (§ 5; utils/regdelta_engine.py; utils/rule_alignment.py; utils/semantic_diff.py; utils/impact_propagation.py); a fixed-denominator quality budget with an integer floor and reconciled cohorts, and a decision-material claim classification, both defined and tested but not wired into the stages (utils/quality_budget.py; utils/claim_admission.py); the documented limit that scope dimensions outside a hard-coded allowlist are refused (§ 5.1); and the repository's own stated limits (technical-report/report.tex § Scope and limitations). Does not support: any measurement from the documented runs, including the rejection rate reported in ARCHITECTURE.md §§ 1.1 and 2.3; any general error rate for language-model extraction; any claim about document or OCR extraction accuracy; any claim about runtime enforcement, releases, approval, activation, promotion, rollback, per-run pinning or a knowledge registry (the repository has none); the counts in quality-baselines/, the refinement counts, compile rates or research results unless this entry is widened to name them; or any claim about systems other than the documented runs.
